human_note: Current is current; future is future. Public ambiguity is not permitted.

statutory_filings: Use the signatory required by the form, law, resolution, or filing instruction; never infer. Duke Y. Demayo signs as President of record where the instrument requires the registered President.

output_rules: Only active officers appear as current.
Future-only people appear only when explicitly labeled planned or future.
Canonical signature blocks are governance artifacts.
failure_modes: CEO signs the Secretary Certificate itself
Duke Y. Demayo omitted as President of record on statutory instruments that require the registered President
CIO expanded as Chief Information Officer instead of Chief Investment Officer
rendered document title borrowed from a different active officer's declared titles (the specific defect Section 41 exists to catch)
registered_officers_of_record: Duke Y. Demayo — director/incorporator; President and Principal of record; serves operationally as COO
Michael C. Silla — director/incorporator, Treasurer, and Corporate Secretary as reflected in incorporation records; CFO title reflected in current records
Ronnie S. del Castillo — Chief Executive Officer, reflected in the recent GIS amendment restoring the original partnership structure
Shieldon Tirazona — Chief Investment Officer, reflected in the recent GIS amendment
planned_governance_display_rule: Leo Ollera and Manny Borres remain non-operational partners and must not be presented as officers or registered officers of record. The active four-officer roster (del Castillo, Demayo, Silla, Tirazona) is current and may be presented as such.
authority_evidence_rule: Titles, signatory powers, and banking authority must be supported by the latest executed board resolutions, minutes, Secretary’s Certificates, bylaws, bank mandates, and SEC filings, including the recent GIS amendment. Marketing profiles and unsigned templates do not create authority.
known_conflicts: Legacy files may still present Duke Y. Demayo as CEO; the current roster places Ronnie S. del Castillo as CEO and Duke Y. Demayo as President/COO. Use the current roster.
Legacy files may present Ronnie S. del Castillo as Chairman/Principal Director; the current public-facing role is Chief Executive Officer.
Statutory and SEC instruments must continue to reflect Duke Y. Demayo as President of record; do not substitute the CEO where the President of record is required.

RESOLVED 2026-09-21 (kernel 2.14.0): the universal quotation master's own hardcoded signoff block printed Duke Y. Demayo with the title "Chief Executive Officer · President · Principal" -- a title that has belonged to Ronnie S. del Castillo since at least kernel 2.1.1. Corrected to "President · Principal · Chief Operating Officer", matching active_officers.duke_y_demayo.titles exactly. The signatory NAME was not changed; only the title string. See Section 41 for the durable check.
section_41_measured_note: Run 2026-09-21 against the real hydrated 2.14.0 derivative: all seven Section 41 checks PASS. Verified by five controls: the corrected build passes; re-injecting the exact original defect (Chief Executive Officer on Duke Y. Demayo) correctly FAILS; a future-only person shown as signatory correctly FAILS; an unrecognised name correctly FAILS; and a genuine SUBSET of the officer's declared titles (President · Principal, dropping COO) correctly PASSES -- proving the check is a real subset/ownership test, not string equality.
multi_signature_rule: Section 41 iterates EVERY signature block in a document as of runtime 1.7. Through 1.6 it used a first-match search and checked only the first, so a two-party instrument -- a CMSA, an SMSA, a countersigned acceptance -- had every block after the first unexamined. The universal quotation master carries one block, so this was latent rather than live; it is fixed before the first two-party derivative rather than after it. ENFORCED as of 2.16.0: Section 43 now runs Section 41 and requires the number of signature blocks it examines to equal the number present in the document. Through 1.7 this was "checked" by a helper that returned a constant string, so the test was true by construction and would have passed with Section 41 deleted.
